mainTopic: Lost items found in a wall and in a rented house: who keeps them?
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion: an item found very rusted has clearly been in the wall a long time. The גמרא then quotes the משנה's rule for a new wall: items in the outer half go to the finder, and items in the inner half go to the בעל הבית. רב אשי adds that a knife follows its handle and a pouch follows its strings. The גמרא explains that the משנה's half-wall rule is for items with no direction, like rags or metal strips. A ברייתא teaches that if the hollow is full of items, the two sides split them, even if it slopes to one side. Next the משנה says that in a house rented to others, the finder keeps what he finds. The גמרא challenges this from money found in ירושלים: shouldn't the items go to the last renter? Three answers follow: an inn for three Jews (ריש לקיש), an inn for three non-Jews (רב מנשיא בר יעקב), and three Jews where the owner gives up hope (רב נחמן). The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting another ruling of רב נחמן that matches his view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The item is very rusted
steps.stepSummary: The closing answer of the earlier discussion: the found item is extremely rusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the item is very rusted.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish the discussion from the previous page. The גמרא answers that the item found is very rusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heavy rust shows the item has been sitting in the wall for a very long time. So it cannot belong to the current בעל הבית. It is treated as old and ownerless, and the finder may keep it.

phrases.english: Where it is very rusted.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer to a question asked at the end of the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the discussion carried over from the previous page.
steps.terutzMaskana: The item is so rusted that it clearly has been there a long time, so it does not belong to the current owner.

steps.title: The rule for a new wall: outer half or inner half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. In a new wall, items in the outer half belong to the finder, and items in the inner half belong to the בעל הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a new wall: from its middle outward, it belongs to the finder. From its middle inward, it belongs to the homeowner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about finding items in a new wall. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new wall cannot hold ancient items, so the question is who hid the item recently. The outer half faces the public, so a passerby probably hid it there. The inner half faces the house, so the בעל הבית probably hid it there.

phrases.english: In a new wall:
from its middle and outward, it is his,
from its middle and inward, it is the homeowner's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new wall instead of an old one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a new wall, items in the outer half go to the finder, and items in the inner half go to the homeowner.

steps.title: רב אשי: a knife follows its handle, a pouch follows its strings
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches that a knife found in a wall is judged by its handle, and a money pouch by its strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a knife goes after its handle, and a pouch goes after its strings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different way to decide who owns certain items found in a wall: look at which way they point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person hides a knife, he holds the handle and pushes the blade in first. So the handle points toward the side he was standing on. The same goes for a pouch's strings. If it points inward, it belongs to the בעל הבית. If it points outward, it belongs to the finder.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A knife goes after the handle,
phrases.notes: Whichever side the handle faces, that is the side of the person who put it there.

phrases.english: and a pouch goes after its strings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: סַכִּינָא בָּתַר קַתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a direction test for certain items found in the wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ownership of a knife or pouch found in a wall depends on which way its handle or strings face.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a clear sign on the item itself can be stronger than a general guess based on where it was found.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the half-wall rule?
steps.stepSummary: If direction decides ownership, the גמרא asks why the משנה splits the wall in half. It should simply look at which way the handle or strings point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about the משנה, which teaches outer half to the finder and inner half to the homeowner? Let us instead see whether the handle faces in or out, or whether the strings face in or out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's rule using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה decides ownership only by which half of the wall the item was in. If direction is the real test, the half-wall rule seems pointless. The גמרא asks why the משנה ignores the item's direction.

phrases.english: But then, the משנה that teaches:
from its middle and outward, it is his,
from its middle and inward, it is the homeowner's?

phrases.aramaic: וְלֶחְזֵי, אִי קַתָּא לְגָאו אִי קַתָּא לְבַר!
phrases.english: Let us see whether the handle faces in or the handle faces out!

phrases.aramaic: אִי שִׁנְצֵיהּ לְגָאו אִי שִׁנְצֵיהּ לְבַר!
phrases.english: Whether its strings face in or its strings face out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's rule from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's direction rule as it fits with the משנה's half-wall rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If direction decides ownership, the משנה should judge by direction and not by which half of the wall the item was in.

steps.title: The משנה is about rags and metal strips
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about items with no handle or strings, such as rags or strips of metal, which have no direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about rags and metal strips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה is speaking about items that have no front or back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rags and metal strips have no handle or strings, so direction tells us nothing. For items like these, the only clue is which half of the wall they were in. So both rules are true, and each one covers different kinds of items.

keyTerms.meaning: rags, scraps of wool or cloth
a strip or bar of metal

steps.whatToRemember: In a new wall, items with a direction (a knife, a pouch) follow which way they point. Items with no direction (rags, metal strips) follow which half of the wall they were in.

phrases.english: The משנה is talking about rags and metal strips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to certain items.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's half-wall rule seemed to cover every item, which would clash with רב אשי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only items with no direction, and רב אשי covers items that have a handle or strings.

steps.title: A wall hollow full of items is split
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the hollow in the wall is filled with items, the finder and the בעל הבית divide them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if the wall was filled with them, they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a new case to the משנה's rule of splitting the wall in half: a hollow completely full of items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items fill both the outer half, which goes to the finder, and the inner half, which goes to the בעל הבית. So the two of them share. This builds on the half-and-half rule from the משנה in Step 2.

phrases.english: It was taught: If the wall was
filled with them, they divide.
phrases.notes: "They" means the finder and the בעל הבית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא case that builds on the משנה's half-and-half rule for walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wall hollow is full of items, the finder and the בעל הבית split them.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to teach something so obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא's rule seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the items fill both halves of the wall, then of course each side gets its half under the משנה's rule. So what does the ברייתא add?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge that a teaching adds nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a filled wall is divided
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's half-and-half rule already covers this, so the ברייתא seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The case is a hollow that slopes to one side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for a hollow that slopes to one side. We might have thought all the items started on the high side and slid down, but the ברייתא teaches that they are still split.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the hollow slopes to one side. You might have said that the items simply slid over from the higher side. So the ברייתא teaches us that they still divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a sloping hollow, where we might have given everything to one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sloped hollow, someone could argue that all the items were first placed on the high side and later slid down to fill the whole space. If so, they would all belong to whoever owns the high side. The ברייתא rejects that idea and still divides the items, so the teaching is not obvious after all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (introduces a special case)
You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: It is needed only where it slopes to one side,
you might have said:
they simply slid down,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פְּשִׁיטָא challenge in Step 7 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a sloped hollow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a sloped hollow, all the items started on the high side and slid down, so they all belong to that side.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not assume they slid. The items are split even in a sloped hollow.
steps.whatToRemember: Even when the hollow slopes, we don't assume the items slid from one side. The finder and the בעל הבית split them.

steps.title: A house rented to others: the finder keeps the items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the owner rents the house out to others, even items found inside the house belong to the finder.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he would rent it out to others, even if one found items inside the house, they belong to the finder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a house that is rented out to many different people. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually items found inside a house belong to the בעל הבית. Here so many people have lived in the house that we cannot tell who lost the item, so the finder keeps it.

phrases.english: If he would rent it out to others,
even if he found it inside the house,
these belong to him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the finder, not the owner of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a house rented to many people, the finder keeps whatever he finds, even inside the house.

steps.title: Why not give it to the last renter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the finder keeps the items. We should assume they belong to the most recent renter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us follow the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the item should go to the most recent renter rather than to the finder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if many people lived in the house, the last renter is the most likely one to have dropped it. So the גמרא suggests we should give it back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us follow the last one

phrases.english: But why?
Let us follow the last one.
phrases.notes: He means the most recent renter of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the finder keeps items found in a rented house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The most recent renter is the most likely owner, so the item should be given to him.

steps.title: Support from money found in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a משנה about money found in ירושלים. Whether the money counts as מעשר שני or חולין depends on who was most likely there and dropped it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn: money found in front of the animal merchants is always treated as מעשר שני. Money found on the הר הבית is חולין. Money found elsewhere in ירושלים during the rest of the year is חולין, but during the רגל, all of it is treated as מעשר שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to support the idea of judging found money by the people who were most recently there. Its point will be spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה decides the status of found money by looking at who usually spends time in that place, and when. People buy animals with מעשר שני money, so money near the animal merchants is treated as מעשר שני. In the city, it depends on the time of year: during the רגל crowds come with מעשר שני money, while during the rest of the year most money is חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a supporting source)
Here: מעשר שני money, which must be spent in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: The money found on the הר הבית is חולין even during the רגל. This is a separate case from the rest of ירושלים, so don't mix the two up.

phrases.english: Didn't we learn:
money found in front of the animal merchants
is always מעשר שני,
on the Temple Mount, it is ordinary money;
and elsewhere in Jerusalem, during the rest of the year, it is ordinary money.
During the festival, all of it is מעשר שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to strengthen the challenge in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that found items should be judged by the most recent people who were in that place
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים 7:2 about money found in ירושלים
steps.whyThisMatters: This source sets up the idea that we judge found money by the people who were most recently there. That is the basis for the challenge against the משנה's rule about rented houses.

steps.title: Why the money in ירושלים counts as new
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה בר זעירא explains the reason behind the ירושלים ruling: the markets are swept every day, so any money found was dropped recently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמעיה בר זעירא said: What is the reason? Because the markets of ירושלים are swept clean every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues building its proof from step 11 by explaining why the ירושלים ruling works the way it does. This is the reasoning that will power the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day the streets are cleaned, so old coins would already have been picked up. That means any coin lying there now was dropped very recently. So we judge it by the people who were there most recently.

phrases.english: And Rav Shemaya bar Ze'eira said:
What is the reason?
Since the markets of Jerusalem
are regularly swept clean every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שְׁמַעְיָה בַּר זְעֵירָא: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ירושלים משנה brought in step 11, so it can be used against our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that we judge found items by the most recent people who were there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שמעיה בר זעירא's explanation of the משנה about money found in ירושלים: the markets are swept daily.

steps.title: So the items should belong to the last renter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the ירושלים logic to our משנה: earlier renters' items are gone, so what is found belongs to the last renter.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that we say: the earlier ones are gone, and these are new ones. Here too, each earlier renter is gone, and these items belong to the last renter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from ירושלים and throws it back at our משנה as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים we assume old coins are gone and new ones belong to the latest group. In the same way, the earlier renters took their things with them, so anything left should be the last renter's. Then why does the משנה let the finder keep it?

phrases.english: So we see that we say:
each of the earlier ones is gone,
and these are other, new ones.
Here too:
each earlier renter is gone,
and these items belong to the last renter!

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: if we always judge by the most recent people, items in a rented house should go to the last renter, not to the finder.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning from step 12 and uses it to finish the challenge from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that items found in a house rented to others belong to the finder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ירושלים case shows we assume earlier owners' things are gone and what remains belongs to the latest people. So the items should belong to the last renter.

steps.title: The house was an inn for three Jews
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר קפרא, answers that the משנה means a house used as an inn for three Jews at once, so nobody knows whose item it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא: The case is where the owner made his house into an inn for three Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the משנה to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not talking about renters coming one after another. It is talking about an inn where three people stay at the same time. With three possible owners there is no single 'last renter,' and the one who lost it gives up hope of getting it back, so the finder keeps it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Kappara:
For example, where he made it an inn
for three Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ פּוּנְדָּק לִשְׁלֹשָׁה יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about an inn with three guests at once.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was about renters who came one after another, so the last renter would own the items.
steps.terutzMaskana: The house was an inn for three Jews at once, so there is no clear owner, and the finder keeps it.

steps.title: That would mean the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even among Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer proves the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews, which is something the גמרא earlier left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a place where most people are Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a big side effect of ריש לקיש's answer. It treats this as a problem with the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (24a), the גמרא asked whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says a lost item in a place where many people pass belongs to the finder. It also asked whether that applies even where most are Jews. If three Jewish guests already count as 'many' and the finder keeps the item, it would settle both questions in one stroke, and the גמרא is not ready to accept that.
steps.confusionAlert: This 'שמע מינה' is not a happy conclusion. The word אלא in the next step shows the גמרא drops this answer instead of accepting what it would prove.

phrases.english: Learn from this that the halacha
follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
phrases.notes: He holds that an item lost where many people pass belongs to the finder, because the owner gives up hope.

phrases.english: even where most of the people are Jews!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אֲפִילּוּ בְּרוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a far-reaching result from ריש לקיש's answer in step 14, which pushes the גמרא to look for another answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's answer that the inn was for three Jews.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If three Jewish guests are enough for the finder to keep the item, then the open question about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is settled, even where most are Jews. The גמרא does not want the משנה to force that result.

steps.title: Rather, the inn was for three non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר יעקב gives a different answer: the משנה is about an inn for three non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב מנשיא בר יעקב said: The case is where the owner made his house into an inn for three non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops ריש לקיש's answer and gives a new way to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guests are still three people at once, so there is no 'last renter.' But since they are non-Jews, the משנה no longer proves anything about a place where most people are Jews. The question about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: רב מנשיא בר יעקב's answer: the משנה is about an inn for three non-Jews. So the finder keeps the item, and nothing is proven about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in a place where most are Jews. The next step gives another answer, from רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא will change its reading of a משנה to avoid settling a question it wants to keep open.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Menashya bar Ya'akov said:
For example, where he made it an inn
for three non-Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: כְּגוֹן שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ פּוּנְדָּק לִשְׁלֹשָׁה נָכְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's answer, which led to the problem in step 15, with a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different way to limit the case (אוקימתא): an inn for three non-Jews.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's answer about three Jews would have proven the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most are Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inn was for three non-Jews, so the finder keeps the item, and nothing is proven about places where most are Jews.

steps.title: Three Jewish guests, but the owner has given up hope
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the משנה can be about an inn with three Jews. The finder keeps the item because the owner has given up hope, not because of any rule about majorities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: You can even say the house was an inn for three Jews. Why may the finder keep it? Because the one who lost it gives up hope. He tells himself: 'Nobody else was with me except these people. I asked them many times to give it back, and they didn't. Will they give it back now? If they wanted to return it, they would have done so already. Since they haven't, they must plan to steal it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a third answer to the question from step 13. He keeps ריש לקיש's case of three Jews, but he gives it a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, ריש לקיש's answer seemed to prove that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews. רב נחמן avoids that proof. Here the finder keeps the item because of the owner's יאוש: only a few known people could have it, and he assumes they plan to keep it. This has nothing to do with whether most people in the area are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives up hope of getting the item back (יאוש)
Let them return it to me
You can even say (keeps the harder case and still answers)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to explain the inn case: ריש לקיש says three Jews and no one knows whose it is; רב מנשיא בר יעקב says three non-Jews; רב נחמן says three Jews, but the owner has given up hope.
steps.confusionAlert: The owner is not giving up hope because Jews usually steal. His reasoning is narrow: only these few guests could have it, and they ignored his requests, so he assumes they plan to keep it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer lets the גמרא leave the earlier question open: does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling apply even where most people are Jews?

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
You can even say it was an inn for three Jews,
phrases.notes: He keeps ריש לקיש's case from step 14 but gives it a new reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason the finder keeps it?
The one who dropped it gives up hope,
because he says to himself:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי אִינִישׁ אַחֲרִינָא לָא הֲוָה בַּהֲדַי
phrases.english: Now, no other person was here with me
except these people;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרִי קַמַּיְיהוּ כַּמָּה זִמְנֵי לַיהְדְּרוּ לִי,
phrases.english: I told them several times to give it back to me,
and they did not give it back to me,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letter in square brackets here. It's the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and now they are going to give it back?!
If they meant to return it,
they would already have returned it to me,
and the fact that they did not return it to me
shows that they plan to steal it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לִשְׁלֹשָׁה יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third answer to step 13. It goes back to the three-Jews case but avoids the problem raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning (יאוש) for the same case setup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the inn had three Jews, the finder could only keep the item if the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with three Jews, the finder keeps the item because the owner gave up hope, believing the other guests meant to steal it.

steps.title: רב נחמן is consistent with his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב נחמן is following his usual reasoning and begins to quote another ruling of his about someone who saw a סלע coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן follows his usual reasoning, as רב נחמן said: If someone saw a סלע coin...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote another ruling of רב נחמן to show it matches the יאוש reasoning he just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula ואזדא לטעמיה tells us the same principle shows up in another ruling by the same אמורא. The quote is just starting here and continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: And he follows his own usual reasoning

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman follows his usual reasoning,
as Rav Naḥman said:
If one saw a sela coin

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַב נַחְמָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a supporting source showing that רב נחמן's יאוש reasoning in step 17 matches his other rulings.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's reasoning in step 17 that the owner gives up hope.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Another ruling of רב נחמן about one who saw a סלע fall (continues in the next text).
